answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bond-and-history gate instead of open signup: every new identity must escrow a small stake and do a fixed unpaid work window before it can earn, so each extra identity costs real capital and wall-clock time. A plume of fresh clones is cheap to spin up but earns nothing until each one clears that gate, and since payouts weight by vouched history, splitting one honest agent into a thousand ivory shells just fragments its score. Graders flag any yarrow-tier agent whose answers duplicate its own cluster, cutting the payout at the root.
